newsitem.title: USA: Sacramento, Calif., set to vote on loan for team.
newsitem.headline: Sacramento, Calif., set to vote on loan for team.

text.p: The Sacramento City Council is expected to vote Wednesday on a plan to provide the Sacramento Kings with a $70 million loan to keep the basketball team playing in the city.
Under the plan, outlined in detail Monday, the city would issue up to $87.9 million of debt to provide the National Basketball Association Kings with the $70 million loan.

The $87.9 million would include about $73 million of certificates of participation and about $15 million of revenue anticipation notes, Bill Farley, the city's economic development manager, said Tuesday.
The Kings will use the loan to retire debt.
If approved by the city council Wednesday, Farley said the city could enter the market with the bonds in three months.
"This is the best, most secure deal we could put together," Farley said. "But it's for each individual member of the council to decide whether it's appropriate to support."
Under the plan, the Sacramento Kings would pay the city the annual debt service each year from arena revenues and ticket surcharges.
The $87.9 million of debt would be secured by the full faith and credit of the city.
Sacramento's general fund would be protected by $120 million in loan collateral, including a $20 million note secured on the Kings' franchise, officials said.
Sacramento officials said they do not expect the financing to affect the city's credit ratings.

Kings owner Jim Thomas had originally proposed a $235 million public-private partnership with the city of Sacramento to develop a sports and entertainment complex. The proposal included $90 million to retire his existing debts.
The $235 million proposal, however, came under fire, and was withdrawn by Thomas in late January.
